jurisdiction.name: Group of Twenty
jurisdiction.overview: Forum of 19 countries, the European Union and the African Union, with a rotating presidency and no secretariat. Its texts are political commitments.

narrative.summary: G20 trade and digital economy ministers adopted the G20 AI Principles in 2019. Digital ministers' declarations in 2020 (Riyadh), 2021 (Trieste) and 2024 (Maceió) each carry a dedicated AI section, the New Delhi Leaders' Declaration of 2023 has a section on harnessing AI responsibly, and G20 innovation ministers under the 2026 United States presidency adopted a statement with AI pillars and the G20 AI Prosperity Objectives.
narrative.review_notes: Membership is taken from Global Affairs Canada's G20 page, and the African Union's accession from the New Delhi Leaders' Declaration of 9-10 September 2023 on the same site, which gives no exact accession day; the AI Principles come from the Tsukuba ministerial statement published by Japan's Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications. The Osaka Leaders' Declaration (June 2019) and later G20 statements on AI are still pending.

instruments.official_title: G20 AI Principles (Annex to the G20 Ministerial Statement on Trade and Digital Economy, Tsukuba)
instruments.issuing_authority: G20 Trade Ministers and Digital Economy Ministers (Japan 2019 presidency)
instruments.publisher_name: G20 Trade Ministers and Digital Economy Ministers (Japan 2019 presidency)
instruments.current_status: Annex to the G20 Ministerial Statement on Trade and Digital Economy, headed 'G20 Ministerial Meeting on Trade and Digital Economy, June 8-9, 2019, Tsukuba, Ibaraki, Japan'; the month is recorded because the statement gives the two meeting days rather than one date. Paragraph 19: the ministers are 'guided by the G20 AI Principles drawn from the OECD Recommendation on AI, which are attached in Annex and are non-binding'. The Annex says 'The G20 supports the Principles for responsible stewardship of Trustworthy AI in Section 1 and takes note of the Recommendations in Section 2.' Full text from the PDF published by Japan's Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications, one of the co-chairing ministries.
instruments.summary: Principles drawn from the OECD Recommendation on AI and welcomed by G20 trade and digital economy ministers in 2019. Section 1 sets five principles for responsible stewardship of trustworthy AI (inclusive growth, sustainable development and well-being; human-centred values and fairness; transparency and explainability; robustness, security and safety; accountability), which the G20 supports; Section 2 lists national-policy and international-cooperation recommendations, which the G20 takes note of. The text states that the principles are non-binding.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: AI principles endorsed at G20 ministerial level, extending the OECD AI Principles to G20 members that are not OECD adherents.
instruments.evidence_reference: Research pass 2026-10-21: Not re-read in this pass; no correction proposed. Consider legal_status 'declaration' or keep nonbinding_guidance (principles annexed to a ministerial statement).

instruments.official_title: G20 Digital Economy Ministers Meeting – Ministerial Declaration
instruments.english_title: G20 Digital Economy Ministers' Declaration (Saudi Presidency, 2020), with Annex 1: Examples of National Policies to Advance the G20 AI Principles
instruments.summary: Declaration of G20 digital economy ministers under the Saudi presidency. Its first section, 'Trustworthy Artificial Intelligence', reaffirms a human-centred approach to AI and support for the G20 AI Principles; each member commits to advance the Principles in line with national priorities. It welcomes Annex 1, 'Examples of National Policies to Advance the G20 AI Principles', and calls for inclusive multi-stakeholder dialogue on AI. Other sections cover cross-border data flows, smart cities, measurement and security of the digital economy.
instruments.current_status: Adopted by G20 digital economy ministers at their meeting hosted by Saudi Arabia on 22 July 2020. A political declaration; it does not create legal obligations.
instruments.evidence_reference: Read the English PDF on the Saudi Ministry of Communications and IT site (2020 presidency host): date line 'Wednesday, July 22, 2020'; section I 'Trustworthy Artificial Intelligence'; Annex 1 named. Arabic version: https://www.mcit.gov.sa/sites/default/files/g20ss_declaration_g20_digital_economy_ministers_meeting_ar_0.pdf. Annex PDF: https://www.mcit.gov.sa/sites/default/files/examples-of-ai-national-policies.pdf (not opened). curl through the proxy was refused (403); WebFetch worked.

instruments.official_title: Declaration of G20 Digital Ministers: Leveraging Digitalisation for a Resilient, Strong, Sustainable and Inclusive Recovery
instruments.english_title: Declaration of G20 Digital Ministers (Trieste, 2021), with Annex 1: G20 Policy Examples on How to Enhance the Adoption of AI by MSMEs and Start-ups
instruments.summary: Declaration of G20 digital ministers under the Italian presidency. Section ii, 'Leveraging Trustworthy Artificial Intelligence for MSMEs' Inclusiveness and Start-ups' Promotion', reaffirms human-centred, trustworthy AI and the G20 AI Principles, notes low AI uptake among small firms, and commits to strengthening their AI capabilities (data, finance, skills) and to agile approaches such as regulatory sandboxes. Annex 1 sets out G20 policy examples for AI adoption by MSMEs and start-ups. Other sections cover digital government, children online, data flows and connectivity.
instruments.current_status: Adopted by G20 digital ministers meeting in Trieste, Italy, on 5 August 2021. A political declaration; it does not create legal obligations.
instruments.evidence_reference: Read the PDF linked from the Italian Department for Digital Transformation page (dated 05 August 2021). The PDF has no separate date line; text states the ministers met in Trieste on 5 August 2021. Section ii and Annex 1 confirmed.

instruments.english_title: G20 New Delhi Leaders' Declaration (section: Harnessing Artificial Intelligence (AI) Responsibly for Good and for All)
instruments.summary: Leaders' declaration of the New Delhi summit. Under 'Technological Transformation and Digital Public Infrastructure' it has a sub-section, 'Harnessing Artificial Intelligence (AI) Responsibly for Good and for All' (paragraph 61), in which leaders commit to use AI responsibly, inclusively and in a human-centric way; to address human rights, transparency, fairness, accountability, safety, human oversight, privacy and data protection; to reaffirm the 2019 G20 AI Principles; to pursue a pro-innovation, risk-aware governance approach; and to promote responsible AI for the Sustainable Development Goals.
instruments.current_status: Adopted by G20 leaders at the New Delhi summit, 9–10 September 2023. A political declaration; it does not create legal obligations.
instruments.evidence_reference: Read on the Indian MEA site (2023 presidency). Printed line: 'New Delhi, India, 9-10 September 2023' (summit dates; no separate adoption date printed, so month only). The MEA PDF carries a running header 'Zero Draft' on its pages although it is the copy released as the adopted declaration; flag for reviewer. AI sub-section is one paragraph (61) under its own heading, plus passing mentions in paras 24(i) and 30(iii).

instruments.official_title: G20 Ministerial Declaration: 13 September, 2024 (G20 Maceió Ministerial Declaration on Digital Inclusion for All)
instruments.english_title: G20 Digital Economy Ministerial Declaration, Maceió (2024)
instruments.summary: Declaration of G20 digital economy ministers under the Brazilian presidency. Its section 'Artificial intelligence for inclusive sustainable development and inequality reduction' reaffirms the G20 AI Principles and the UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of AI, commits to risk-based, human-centric, development-oriented and innovation-friendly AI governance, calls for international cooperation and capacity building to avoid widening digital divides, encourages AI use to improve public services, and welcomes presidency deliverables including a Toolkit for AI Readiness and Capacity Assessment.
instruments.current_status: Adopted by G20 digital economy ministers meeting in Maceió, Brazil, on 13 September 2024. A political declaration; it does not create legal obligations.
instruments.evidence_reference: Read the full text on GOV.UK (UK government, a G20 member; published 14 September 2024). The text states ministers convened in Maceió on 13 September 2024. The Brazilian presidency site (gov.br/g20) was not reachable in the first pass. Title on GOV.UK is 'G20 Ministerial Declaration: 13 September, 2024'; the commonly used title 'Maceió Ministerial Declaration on Digital Inclusion for All' was not confirmed on an official page.
